question_text: A regional bank gives every branch new tablets for opening accounts. Staff still print each form, collect a signature on paper and file it in a cabinet, exactly as before. Why is this not yet digital transformation?
hint: The slide names three things that are equally important.
correct_answer_citation: Technology is a key enabler, but people and processes are equally important.

options.option_text: The technology changed, but the people and processes did not.
options.option_explanation: Right. Technology is a key enabler, but people and processes are equally important. The tablets changed nothing about how the bank operates.

options.option_text: The bank bought tablets instead of more powerful computers.
options.option_explanation: Better hardware would not help. The way staff work stays the same whatever device they hold.

options.option_text: Only some areas of a bank can use digital technology.
options.option_explanation: Digital transformation is the integration of digital technology into all areas of a business, a bank included.

options.option_text: Digital transformation is complete once every branch has the new technology.
options.option_explanation: Owning the technology is not the change. Transformation changes how the business operates and delivers value to customers.

prompt: Six organizations are changing how they work. Name the key component of digital transformation each case shows.

cases.text: A grocery chain fits its delivery vans with IoT sensors and moves its stock records to the cloud.
cases.explanation: It adopts advanced technologies (IoT, cloud computing) to streamline its operations.

cases.text: A hospital's managers praise teams that try new ideas, even when some of the trials fail.
cases.explanation: It builds a mindset of innovation and experimentation among employees.

cases.text: A hotel uses each guest's past stays to offer the room type and breakfast that guest usually prefers.
cases.explanation: It uses insight into customer preferences to deliver a personalized experience.

cases.text: An insurer redesigns its claims handling so that routine claims are approved automatically.
cases.explanation: It reengineers a business process and automates a routine task to remove inefficiency.

cases.text: A bakery chain studies sales by store and by hour before it sets new opening times.
cases.explanation: It collects and analyzes data to make an informed decision.

cases.text: When a new payment app suddenly becomes popular, a café chain accepts it at every till within a month.
cases.explanation: It adapts quickly to a new technology and to changing customer demands.

prompt: Sort each organizational change into the stage it belongs to.

cards.text: A library scans its paper card catalogue into PDF files.
cards.explanation: Analog information is converted into digital format: digitize information.

cards.text: A clinic types its handwritten patient notes into files sorted by patient name.
cards.explanation: The information is digitized and organized; nothing about the work itself changes yet.

cards.text: A school photographs its old exam papers and stores them as image files.
cards.explanation: Paper becomes digital files: digitize information.

cards.text: An accounting firm sets its software to send every client's invoice automatically each month.
cards.explanation: A process that staff did by hand is now automated.

cards.text: A warehouse links its order system to its shipping system, so orders no longer have to be typed in twice.
cards.explanation: The process is streamlined; the business itself stays the same.

cards.text: A company replaces paper holiday requests with an online form that routes each request to the right manager.
cards.explanation: An existing process is automated and streamlined.

cards.text: A video-rental chain closes its stores and rebuilds itself as a streaming subscription service.
cards.explanation: It rethinks its business model and creates a new value proposition: the institution is transformed.

cards.text: A taxi firm becomes an app where riders book, track and pay for any nearby driver.
cards.explanation: It goes beyond digitization: the business model and the customer experience change.

prompt: Match each layer of the pyramid with the initiative that belongs to it.

pairs.match: A retailer moves its servers to the cloud and adds protection against cyberattacks.
pairs.explanation: Cloud computing and cybersecurity are technology infrastructure.

pairs.match: A bank sets rules on who may use customer data and builds dashboards to analyse it.
pairs.explanation: Data governance and analytics tools sit in the data layer.

pairs.match: A factory automates the workflow that approves each purchase order.
pairs.explanation: Workflow automation re-engineers a business process.

pairs.match: An airline redesigns its booking app so travellers can change a seat in two taps.
pairs.explanation: User experience design improves the customer experience through a digital channel.

pairs.match: A new CEO runs a change programme and trains every employee in digital skills.
pairs.explanation: Change management and employee training belong to culture and leadership.

pairs.match: A carmaker partners with startups to experiment with new business models.
pairs.explanation: Experimentation and partnerships with startups explore new business models.
